correctness.rationale: Substituting g=0 and F(x)=ax, a>0, in the two-step constant-reflection scheme gives A=1-(1+alpha)t and B=alpha*t with t=a*tau>0, x[k+1]=A x[k]+B x[k-1]. The monic polynomial z^2-Az-B has one positive and one negative real root; Jury inequalities 1-A-B=t>0, 1+A-B=2-(1+2alpha)t>0 and 1+B>0 give exact Schur stability 0<t<2/(1+2alpha). For x[-1]=x[0]!=0, x1/x0=1-t cannot equal a root since p(1-t)=-alpha*t^2!=0, so the unstable boundary mode cannot cancel. The spectral factor is (sqrt(A^2+4B)+|A|)/2. For A>=0 the dominant root derivative has sign alpha-(1+alpha)q, negative because its root is strictly greater than alpha/(1+alpha) (evaluate polynomial there). For A<=0 derivative is positive. Thus the unique minimizer is t*=1/(1+alpha), q*=sqrt(alpha/(1+alpha)); the scalar stability ceiling decreases and the optimal factor increases with alpha. Independent numerical checks for alpha=0.501,0.7,1,2,4 and boundary/near-optimal steps corroborate the algebra; no finite test proves all alpha.
